sentences.text: Pachyrhinosaurus is a genus of three species of ceratopsian dinosaurs, classified within the subfamily Centrosaurinae of the family Ceratopsidae. The genus was named by Charles M. Sternberg in 1950.
The largest species, P. canadensis, is estimated to reach lengths of 6 to 8 meters and weigh 3 to 4 tonnes.
In 2024, a 138 cm long skull of P. lakustai with a 43 cm diameter nasal boss was unearthed at Pipestone Creek and nicknamed "Big Sam".
One skull known as "Harvey" displayed a massive lesion 195 millimeters wide on its right face that likely caused blindness in that eye.
Despite its robust appearance, it may have been able to run at 9 meters per second, about 32 km/h.
Excavations revealed more than 100 bones per square meter, a total of 3,500 bones, and 14 skulls.

The first examples of Pachyrhinosaurus were discovered by Charles M. Sternberg in Alberta, Canada, in 1946, and the genus was named in 1950. The holotype and paratype skulls of P. canadensis were collected in 1945 and 1946 from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.
A large bonebed of Pachyrhinosaurus was found in 1974 by Al Lakusta along Pipestone Creek in Alberta.
Pachyrhinosaurus was herbivorous and possessed strong cheek teeth batteries for cutting tough, fibrous plants. It had a sharp beak used to cut the plants it fed on.
The nasal boss of P. perotorum bore a thick, cornified pad and sheath, representing a unique integumentary feature not seen in other species.
This feature was likely used for locking and pushing in intraspecific combat, similar to muskoxen.
The presence of skeletons ranging from juveniles to adults in the Pipestone Creek bonebed suggests that Pachyrhinosaurus cared for its young.
Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum reached 28% of its adult body size by the age of one year and was nearly half the size of a mature adult by the age of two.

In the ecosystem of the St. Mary River Formation, the tyrannosaurid Albertosaurus was likely the apex predator alongside Pachyrhinosaurus. In the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, the tyrannosaurid Albertosaurus sarcophagus was the apex predator of the paleoenvironment.
In the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, hadrosaurs dominated the dinosaur population, making up half of all dinosaurs in the region.
Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai lived from about 73.5 to 72.5 million years ago.
Fossils from the St. Mary River Formation range geographically from Glacier County, Montana, to the Little Bow River in Alberta.
The Horseshoe Canyon Formation, another source of Pachyrhinosaurus fossils, has been dated between 74 and 67 million years old.

It was previously thought that P. perotorum had unique forward-projecting horns, but 2019 research showed these were inaccurately reconstructed and it actually had backward-pointing horns like its sister species.
Scientists are not very sure if it had a nasal horn because no complete skulls have been found.
